spec.description: The National Weather Service's Local Storm Reports of the past seven days across the United States, live from NOAA's public ArcGIS service: tornadoes, hail, wind, floods and snow on a map with a time player, density hexbins and a casualties layer, and counts by type and state that follow the map's extent.

options.content:
# Severe weather reports — NOAA / National Weather Service

A replica on this panel of [Esri's ArcGIS dashboard](https://www.arcgis.com/apps/dashboards/94054353efa943b781cc5d6176ca8283),
on the same data and live: the *Local Storm Reports* that the 122 forecast offices of the NWS
publish every day, aggregated by Esri into a public Feature Service.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Source** | `NOAA_storm_reports_v1/FeatureServer/4` — *ALL Storm Reports (past week)*, no token |
| **Pipeline** | Infinity → `f=json` → `latitude`/`longitude`/`time` columns → the panel detects them and kepler draws |
| **Coverage** | rolling 7-day window · one request, no pagination |
| **Licence** | public domain (NOAA); service hosted by Esri |

**Everything beside and below the map is computed for what is on screen** — pan or zoom and the
counts follow. The time player under the map narrows them further. `MAGNITUDE` mixes units by type
(inches, knots, EF number), so it is in the tooltip and drives no point size.

params.value: LONGITUDE BETWEEN $west AND $east AND LATITUDE BETWEEN $south AND $north AND INCIDENT_TYPE IN (${type:sqlstring}) AND STATE IN (${state:sqlstring})

spec.description: Reported casualties, summed per day on the server — `CAST(INCIDENT_DATETIME AS DATE)` as the group, so this costs one 300-byte request rather than bucketing 1.951 rows in the browser. **Expect it to be empty most weeks**: casualties appear on roughly 6 reports in 2.000, and a flat zero line here is the true answer, not a broken panel. Follows the map's extent and both pickers; deliberately *not* the player's window, so the brush has a shape to move over. Day buckets are UTC and the finest the service offers.
spec.title: Deaths and injuries per day

params.value: (FATALITIES > 0 OR INJURIES > 0) AND INCIDENT_DATETIME IS NOT NULL

spec.description: Always fetches the whole week. It reads neither the extent variables nor the player's: if it did, zooming out would not bring the rows back — the dataset would no longer hold them. The extent and the brush are masks over data that stays whole.
spec.title: Severe weather reports — last 7 days

body_form.value: HOURS_OLD <= 24 AND LONGITUDE BETWEEN $west AND $east AND LATITUDE BETWEEN $south AND $north AND INCIDENT_TYPE IN (${type:sqlstring}) AND STATE IN (${state:sqlstring})

spec.description: The 24-hour column of the ArcGIS dashboard, in a single request: six `CASE` expressions inside `outStatistics`. A type with no events returns 0 rather than disappearing. Sent as `POST` for the same reason as the block below — with every state picked this query is 1.958 characters as a `GET`, and the ceiling is 2.048.
spec.title: Last 24 hours

spec.description: The same, for the span the map's time brush marks. With no brush the `mapFrom` / `mapTo` guards span everything and the block shows the whole week. Sent as `POST`: with every state picked and a brush set, the `GET` form is 2.186 characters of query string and Esri answers **404** above 2.048.
spec.title: In the player's window

options.content:
**Source:** National Weather Service (NOAA) · service aggregated and hosted by Esri ·
[USA Storm Reports](https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=e109e8fd9c5a495c813b5cbaee9c7d9b)
in the ArcGIS Living Atlas. The reports are **preliminary**; the verified ones live at NOAA's NCEI.

**Deliberate differences from the ArcGIS dashboard.** Its chart is called *State Chart* but groups
by event type; both are here. Its *Rain* indicator queries `INCIDENT_TYPE = 'Heavy Rain'`, a string
that is not in the NWS vocabulary today and therefore always returns 0; *Lightning* and *Wildfire*
take its place. And the time player, the density hexbins, the human-impact layer and the daily
casualty series have no equivalent there.

spec.title: Severe weather reports — NOAA/NWS

spec.description: Filled from the service itself, so the map can never write a value that is not in the list. kepler's filter on `type` and this variable are one state, in two directions.
